newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Early Taiwan dollar edges lower, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Early Taiwan dollar edges lower, seen stable.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar edged lower in early Thursday trade following the local unit's recent uptrend, but dealers said they saw little room for a big fluctuation.
After 30 minutes, at 0130 GMT, the local unit had eased to T$27.863 against Wednesday's T$27.858 close.
Turnover through dealers was a light US$13 million.

A persistent liquidity squeeze in the banking system continued to trigger U.S. dollar sales in exchange for Taiwan dollars, but dealers said the factor was unlikely to fuel a significant Taiwan dollar rebound.
Lingering quarter-end greenback demand would offset those gains, they said.

"Tight liquidity has fuelled the Taiwan dollar's recent rebound, but many investors who bought the U.S. dollar at the previous high level are not willing to sell their position at this moment," said one dealer.
"The rate is likely to be stuck in the current range," the dealer said.
Some dealers said the central bank seemed to prefer a stable Taiwan dollar ahead of Hong Kong's handover to Taipei's rival, communist China -- a politically delicate moment for Taiwan.
A stable T$27.85-90 range was seen for Thursday.
